_comment: Elevation/shadow tier — previously undefined in this token set (see docs/figma-sync.md's former 'known gap'). Sourced fresh from the Buttons page (Lumen-AI-Design-System, node 475:7210)'s 'Raised' button type, the first real component in this file to use elevation. Each 'button' value is a two-layer drop-shadow (a soft ambient layer + a directional layer) read directly off that state's real Figma fill, not extrapolated. 'button.pressed-inset' is a separate inset shadow used by the flat (non-elevated) Primary/Icon-only types specifically on their Active state, to convey a pressed effect without giving them permanent elevation. 'elevation.sm' is the first entry in the generic Elevation/None-Sm-Md-Lg-Xl scale docs/design-tokens.md §6 calls for. Corrected 2026-07-20: originally sourced at 0.04 opacity from the 'appshell-desktop-closed-light' example instance (node 1197:1652, `1102:6521`), then re-verified against the canonical 'AppShell' page's own Breakpoint=Desktop/Theme=Light KPICard instance (node 1007:3700, `1119:3343`) via get_design_context — the authoritative source disagrees with the example instance and specs 0.08 opacity; the canonical value wins per this repo's Figma authority order. Only this one tier is sourced so far; None/Md/Lg/Xl remain unimplemented pending a component that specs them. **2026-08-06**: the full generic scale was found — a live 'Scale / Elevation (Live)' frame (node 1770:7, user-supplied Figma URL) — and added as `elevation.1`-`elevation.5`. Figma's own naming for this scale is numeric (Elevation/1..5), not this doc's aspirational None/Sm/Md/Lg/Xl — `docs/design-tokens.md` §6's naming section should be corrected to match, not the other way around. `elevation.sm` predates this discovery and does NOT match any of the 5 new values byte-for-byte, so it isn't actually part of this real numbered scale despite its name — kept as its own real, KPICard-sourced value rather than folded in or renumbered. `elevation.4` is byte-identical to `modal.default` below (sourced separately on 2026-08-05 from Modal's own 'Elevation/4 — Modal' named effect), confirming that tier really is generic Elevation/4 — not repointed to alias it, since shadow.json's build hasn't been verified to support cross-references the way semantic/color.json does.

default._comment: Exact two-layer drop shadow ('Shadow/sm - y:16') read off Figma node 1475:5100's Toast frame via get_design_context. No existing shadow tier matches this combination.

Figma's own named effect is 'Elevation/4 — Modal' — sourced via get_variable_defs on node 1737:4152 ('Modal' component), 2026-08-05. A distinct, component-scoped tier; doesn't extend the generic elevation.sm scale since no Elevation/1-3 data exists yet to interpolate a real numbered scale from one data point.
